source: She passed away recently. Very recently, in fact.
You're serious? She owed me a small fortune in losings at my table!
How am I to ever recover it now? Good-for-nothing wandering noblewomen...
Goodness. And despite it all, I really did like the woman.
I'd half believe something like this was just another idiot prank of hers.
Oh. Er.
Hamlet, I have something to discuss about Lady Guildenstern.
She's passed away suddenly. I'm sorry to be the one to have to break this to you.
How did she pass? When did this happen?
She, er... she... was... she... drowned. Yes. Drowned.
Off the docks, I'm afraid.
How horrible.
Who let this happen? Where were the guards? Why wasn't anyone watching?
Does Rosie know? If not, she ought to.
And-- I want this investigated at once. I want to know exactly what took place.
I need to understand what happened, first. The rest will follow.
(I feel awful lying to him, but Guilda asked me to...)
There's... something I need to talk with you about.
I'm so sorry to be the one to tell you this, but... Guildenstern has passed away.
She, er, drowned. By the docks.
It came as a surprise to me, too.
This is one of her idiot pranks again, isn't it?
No. No... if you're coming to tell this to me... it must be true.
She's never involved someone else in a prank before.
So it's true, then.
Guilda... I...
(This is cruel.)
What was she doing down by the docks? She can't swim. We both know that.
Ophelia, it's so strange. I know what you're saying is true, but it doesn't feel real.
You know, when my father died it felt the same way. I expected sorrow. But-- nothing. Just nothing.
Just the sense that the bottom's fallen out of the world.
I... I have to make arrangements. No one else will.
Please excuse me.
(I feel awful lying to her, but Guilda asked me to.)
She passed away recently, as you may or may not have known.
Oh. Hmm? Guildenstern? Ah, yes, with the hat. I recall now.
A nice lady. A shame she had to pass so young.
(He didn't seem to particularly care...)
Well, yeh, that's wot happens now an' then! Unfortunate an' sad!
Oh. That Lady Guildenstern? The one from Hamlet's school?
Well, I'm sure he's devastated. I'm sorry to hear it, Ophelia.
I bear some unfortunate information about Lady Guildenstern..
Which one is Guildenstern again?
Ah, never mind it. I was on my way to find something to eat. We can talk about this later.
Ah. I'm sorry to have lost her, Ophelia. She was a good friend to Hamlet.
These things do happen, I suppose.
(She didn't seem to particularly care...)
She's dead?
Ergh. I'll need to think of—something—to—honor her, then.
(And some way to keep an eye on Hamlet...)
I suppose you will.
Ah. I'm sorry to hear it. Seemed to be a nice, pleasant, well-bred lady.
I bear some unfortunate news about Lady Guildenstern.
Oh, really? How?
She, er, drowned.
You're a terrible liar, 'Feely. Your big green eyes give you away instantly.
I-It's that easy to tell?
All I'll say is this: You will never have a career at the card table. Never.
Were it anyone else I might believe you, but Guildenstern's never done a single real thing in her entire life. Or death, for that matter.
So she's gone and faked her death, eh? Can't wait for that to come full circle.
So. This fake death business. There's no chance this goes wrong?
Absolutely not! It's impossible. All of my plans work flawlessly.
And even when they don't, well...
I'm a very fast runner, you know. They'll never catch me.
My lady, you're close to Brit. Do you know what's got her so doom and gloom?
Oh, Brit... I've had just about enough of her lately.
She's been so short-tempered with me—and all because she hasn't heard from her mother since she came here.
Her mother hasn't written her? But she lives just a crow's fly away.
Oh, heavens, she's written Brit, of course! That dratted woman can't stop writing to Brit. A new one comes through the gate nearly every day.
But I hid them all, obviously.
Hid the... letters?
Yes. This is my duty, Ophelia. Brit's father sent her here to become a lady of the court and to set aside childish things.
He warned me Brit would look for every possible excuse to run along home again. But he won't have it. She is to become Lady Brockenhuus.
Hiding Brit's mother's letters was all I could think to do. If she read them, it'd only make her terribly homesick, and what then?
Besides, they were so depressing. 'I wish you'd come home, darling.' 'I wish you'd never left.' Well, I put all those silly letters where unheard wishes go.
'Where unheard wishes go'?
Ooh. Never mind. Forget what I said!
You and Brit both often spend your days in the gallery. Have you spoken to her closely?
Most certainly.
Do you know what ails her?
It is a malady of the soul. Lady Brit and I are kindred spirits in that way, you know.
Did you know she's an artist? And quite a good one, at that. But she's been disallowed from painting.
Artists who aren't doing work waste all their time being poisonously jealous of those who are.
It's a shame about all her oils. I wonder if she'll ever get them back.
Oils? You mean oil... paints?
Yes. When she came here, I understand her father confiscated them all. She wasn't to use them within Elsinore.
I had no idea. Couldn't she have made more?
Of course. New tools are made easily enough, but Brit is not one to ask for help. If you're looking to lend Madame Artiste a hand, I can be of service.
I've got the pigments to make colors, but I'll need bases for the oils, some canvas materials, and some charcoal. Luckily, all highly procurable!
I'll need some eggs, charcoal for sketching, and some linen cloth for canvas.
Linen... I've got a number of undergarments made of the stuff... Hrm.
Let me know when you've found everything, and I'll assist with the finer details.
You know Lady Brit better than most. Do you know what's got her in such a strange mood?
I don't know what to say on the matter of Lady Brit these days.
All I know is, given what you've already told me, I must speak with her immediately.
That will give me a chance to clear the air with her. I'm sure of it.
Now that I know she intended to betray our country and have us all killed, what does it matter?
She lied to us, Ophelia. And most of all, she lied to me. I loved her, and she looked into my eyes and she told me falsehoods.
What kind of twisted person does that? I hardly think I want to know anymore. I'd rather discard her, pretend she never existed.
I wish I had but a moment's peace to be with her.
Right now, though, as things have been proceeding—I don't know when I'll next have that peaceful moment.
(I've caught him too late, it seems.)
What's wrong with Brit?
Did she say something to you?
Not exactly—but something's amiss. I can tell.
I just met with her the other night. She... has a lot on her mind.
I'd give her some space, Ophelia. Let her sort things out.
(Perhaps if I had approached him before this meeting, he would have spoken on my behalf.)
You aren't sailing for Paris?
I was. But Paris will still be there in a week.
My thanks for your excellent timing on this, sister.
Had you caught me a moment later, I'd have left her alone.
Why does Lady Brit act the way she does?
Without impunity, you mean?
Mother tried to get us to be close friends the moment she set foot in this castle. I refused.
On some level, I shall never truly be anything to her other than a tool.
You know Lady Brit better than most. Do you know why she's so ill-tempered?
Aye. She is not here of her own accord.
She was brought here in the name of good will between Denmark's crown and its nobility.
Her family's roots run deeper than any other. Kings and Queens of days long past, and the like.
But despite all the power afforded to her status, she is little more than prisoner to it.
You of all women ought to understand that.
Cygnus at the town gate is acting strangely. Something about being 'on thin ice' and 'winnings.' Do you know why?
Ah... ah... I don' know!
Don' look at me with those big angry eyes! I won't talk for no one!
(All right, so clearly the answer is yes, but he won't tell me.)
(Then who?)
Irma, the guard at the town gate mentioned something odd. Something to do with 'recouping his losses.' Any ideas?
Some fools cannot keep their mouths shut.
This old woman knows differently.
(All right, so clearly the answer is yes, but she won't tell me.)
What have your men been getting up to lately, Bernardo?
Lately? Nothing at all. Of course...
We had some incidents with gambling a few weeks ago. I know they do it, but I've banned them from doing it within the castle.
It's sinful behavior, it leads to a lack of discipline, and I won't stand for it in the guard quarters.
And you're certain they aren't doing it any longer? Cygnus mentioned something about playing 'at night'.
And you're certain they aren't doing it any longer? I've seen Irma heading into the guards' quarters.
...Those idiots.
I'll keep an eye out. And if I see anything in the future...
I will handle it with swift and merciless justice.
I will handle this with swift and merciless justice.
Brit, do you know why the guards would believe they were on 'thin ice' with Bernardo?
All that sneaking about with their dice games, I'm certain. Marcellus and Irma are the ringleaders.
Bernardo banned them from doing it, but that obviously hasn't stopped them, because they're not very smart, which is why they beat things with their fists for a living.
They play in the evenings, I think. In the guard house.
How do you know so much about this?
Uncovering the worst parts of people is my special talent.
Horatio, do you know why the guards would believe they were on 'thin ice' with Bernardo?
What, again?
Irma's reignited their little gambling circle. Against Bernardo's wishes, naturally.
It's impossible to sleep in the guard house on the nights they do it. I've had to curl up in the stables more often than I'd like to admit.
You'd think they'd develop a modicum of discretion about it... but... sadly, that's not their forte.
